title: The Shepherd and the Wild Sheep
story_html:
Once, there was a shepherd. Every night, he gathered and counted his sheep. He made sure never to overlook any of them. One night, he saw some wild sheep had joined his herd. He hoped to acquire the newcomers.

It snowed that night. In the morning, the shepherd couldn't take his sheep out of his lodge. Instead, he had to feed them inside. He gave a small amount of wheat to his own sheep. But he gave more of the food to the wild sheep. He thought the extra wheat would discourage them from leaving.

It snowed for several days. During that time, the shepherd's sheep ate very little. The wild sheep, however, ate very well. At last, the snow melted, and they ventured outdoors. As soon as he opened the door of his hut, the wild sheep started to run away.

"Wait! This is how you repay me? After I treated you so kindly, why do you run away?" the shepherd asked. His voice was full of hatred. The wild sheep stopped and turned toward the shepherd.

"We're leaving because you fed us better than your own sheep," one of the wild sheep replied. "You tried to deceive us with your ridiculous plan. Yesterday, you treated us kindly, but tomorrow you might be different. If more wild sheep joined your herd, you would treat us as inferior sheep."

As the wild sheep ran away, the shepherd understood his offense. He knew this awkward situation was his own fault. He had not been a satisfactory caretaker. He was a fake friend to the wild sheep. Because of this, he had neglected his own sheep.

questions.q: What did the shepherd do every night?
opts: He gathered and counted his sheep
He fed the wild sheep wheat
He locked the wild sheep in a hut
He sold some of his sheep

questions.q: What did the shepherd hope to do when wild sheep joined his herd?
opts: Chase them away
Sell them at the market
Acquire the newcomers for his own herd
Return them to another shepherd

questions.q: Why did the shepherd have to feed his sheep inside?
opts: The sheep were sick
There was no grass in the field
Wolves were near the lodge
It had snowed, so he couldn't take them outside

questions.q: Why did the shepherd give more wheat to the wild sheep?
opts: Because they were bigger and hungrier
Because he thought the extra food would discourage them from leaving
Because his own sheep didn't like wheat
Because the wild sheep asked him for it

questions.q: What happened as soon as the shepherd opened the door of his hut?
opts: The wild sheep started to run away
The wild sheep thanked the shepherd
His own sheep ran away
It began to snow again

questions.q: In the story, the word 'repay' means:
opts: to run away quickly
to count something again
to feed hungry animals
to give something back in return for kindness

questions.q: Why did the wild sheep decide to leave?
opts: Because the shepherd's voice was full of hatred
Because he fed them better than his own sheep, so they did not trust him
Because the lodge was too cold in winter
Because they wanted to find more wheat

questions.q: What did the wild sheep think would happen if more wild sheep joined the herd?
opts: They would get more food than before
They would be sold to another farm
They would be treated as inferior sheep
They would be locked inside the hut

questions.q: What did the shepherd understand at the end of the story?
opts: That the awkward situation was his own fault
That the wild sheep were ungrateful
That he needed a bigger lodge
That wheat was bad for sheep

questions.q: Why can the shepherd be called a 'fake' friend to the wild sheep?
opts: He never gave the wild sheep any food
He shouted at the wild sheep every day
He told lies about the wild sheep to others
His kindness was not honest — he only wanted to keep them for himself
